subject: Archaeology
title: The Roman Forum: Heart of an Empire
description: A quick, practical guide to The Roman Forum: Heart of an Empire.

hook.text: The political center of the Roman Empire was once a swamp. They drained it and built the world's most famous plaza.

buildup.text: The Forum held temples, law courts, and the Senate house. Every triumph, trial, and speech happened here.

discovery.text: Caesar was cremated in the Forum. Augustus built a temple on the exact spot where his body was burned.

twist.text: After Rome fell, the Forum became a cow pasture for a thousand years. Locals called it 'Campo Vaccino.'

climax.text: Excavations began in the 1800s. Layer by layer, the center of the ancient world re-emerged from beneath farmland.

punchline.text: The heart of an empire spent a millennium as a cow field.

quiz.question: What happened to the Roman Forum after the empire fell?
options: It was converted into a Christian cathedral complex
It became a cow pasture called Campo Vaccino for centuries
It was buried by a volcanic eruption from nearby hills
